chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from Yāsir, who said:

When al-Maʾmūn departed from Khurāsān intending Baghdād, and al-Faḍl, the one with the two authorities, departed, and we departed with Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام, a letter from his brother al-Ḥasan ibn Sahl came to al-Faḍl ibn Sahl, the one with the two authorities, while we were at one of the stopping places: “I examined the turning of the year in the calculation of the stars, and I found in it that in such-and-such a month, on Wednesday, you will taste the heat of iron and the heat of fire. I think that you, Amīr al-Muʾminīn, and al-Riḍā should enter the bathhouse on this day, perform cupping there, and pour the blood over your hands so that its ill fortune may depart from you.”

So the one with the two authorities wrote to al-Maʾmūn about that and asked him to ask Abū al-Ḥasan about it. Then al-Maʾmūn wrote to Abū al-Ḥasan asking him that, and Abū al-Ḥasan wrote back to him: “I will not enter the bathhouse tomorrow, and I do not think that you or al-Faḍl should enter the bathhouse tomorrow.” Then he sent the note back to him twice.

Then Abū al-Ḥasan wrote to him: “O Amīr al-Muʾminīn, I will not enter the bathhouse tomorrow, for I saw the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم in sleep this night, and he said to me: ‘O ʿAlī, do not enter the bathhouse tomorrow.’ And I do not think that you or al-Faḍl should enter the bathhouse tomorrow.” So al-Maʾmūn wrote to him: “You have spoken the truth, my master, and the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم has spoken the truth. I will not enter the bathhouse tomorrow, and al-Faḍl knows best.”

He said: Yāsir said: “When evening came and the sun had set, al-Riḍā عليه السلام said to us: ‘Say: We seek refuge in Allah from the evil of what descends on this night.’ So we continued saying that. Then when al-Riḍā عليه السلام had performed the morning salat (prayer), he said to me: ‘Climb onto the roof and listen carefully; do you hear anything?’”

So when I climbed up, I heard the uproar, and it intensified and increased. Then al-Maʾmūn entered through the door leading to his house from the house of Abū al-Ḥasan, saying: ‘O my master, O Abū al-Ḥasan, may Allah reward you concerning al-Faḍl. He refused, entered the bathhouse, and some people came upon him with swords and killed him. Three of those who entered upon him were seized, and one of them was his maternal cousin al-Faḍl ibn Dhī al-Qalamayn.’

He said: “Then the soldiers, commanders, and the men of al-Faḍl gathered at al-Maʾmūn’s door and said: ‘This one assassinated him and killed him’—meaning al-Maʾmūn—‘and we will demand his blood.’ They brought fires to burn the door. Then al-Maʾmūn said to Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام: ‘My master, do you think you could go out to them and disperse them?’”

He said: Yāsir said: “So Abū al-Ḥasan mounted and said to me: ‘Mount.’ So I mounted. When we came out from the door of the house, he looked at the people while they had crowded together, and he gestured to them with his hand: ‘Disperse, disperse.’ Yāsir said: ‘Then the people turned away—by Allah, some of them fell over others—and he did not gesture to anyone except that he ran off and passed on.’”

key_terms.اغْتَالَهُ: assassinated him; accusation made against al-Maʾmūn
key_terms.الضَّجَّةَ: the uproar and commotion heard before the news arrived
key_terms.الْحَمَّامَ: the bathhouse central to the warning and ensuing event
key_terms.تَفَرَّقُوا: disperse; the Imam’s command to the crowd
key_terms.حِسَابِ النُّجُومِ: astrological calculation mentioned in the letter
key_terms.رَسُولَ اللَّهِ صَلَّى اللَّهُ عَلَيْهِ: the Prophet seen in a dream giving instruction
key_terms.نَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ: a formula of seeking refuge in Allah

ai.seo_question: How did Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام foretell the death of al-Faḍl ibn Sahl and calm the people afterward?
ai.summary: This narration recounts how Imam al-Riḍā عليه السلام warned against entering the bathhouse on a particular day, after a dream in which the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم instructed him not to do so. The account then describes the killing of al-Faḍl ibn Sahl, the unrest that followed, and how the Imam عليه السلام calmed the crowd by his presence and gesture.
